o: A stable subarray contains no inversion, so it must live entirely inside one maximal non-decreasing block of nums. Within a block every subarray is stable. For a query [l, r] the answer is Σ min(c[i], i - l + 1) over i in [l, r], where c[i] is the length of the non-decreasing run ending at i: runs extending left of l get truncated at l. Since run-start positions d[i] = i - c[i] + 1 are non-decreasing, a binary search splits the range into a truncated part (arithmetic series) and a full part (prefix sums of c).
k: Stability = containment in one maximal non-decreasing block.
min(c[i], i-l+1) handles truncation at the query's left endpoint; d[i] monotone enables binary search.

a.n: Approach 1: Run-Length DP + Prefix Sums + Binary Search
a.i: Precompute c[i], d[i], prefix sums of c. Each query binary-searches the split point and combines a geometric/arithmetic count with a prefix-sum sum.
s: Compute c[i] (run length ending at i) and d[i] = i - c[i] + 1.
Per query: find first t in [l, r] with d[t] >= l (bisect on d).
a.t: O((n + q) log n) — binary search per query
a.sp: O(n) for the DP and prefix arrays

w: The key leap is rewriting the per-query count as Σ min(c[i], i-l+1); verify on the samples ([3,1,2] query [0,2]: mins are 1,1,2 → 4). Answers can reach ~n²/2, so use 64-bit integers. Follow-up: point updates to nums (would need a segment tree over runs).
